newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India gains on pre-budget buying.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India gains on pre-budget buying.

text.p: Selective position-taking ahead of the forthcoming central budget strengthened prices of Indian global depositary receipts on Wednesday, traders said.
"The demand was moderate but it was across the board," a dealer said.
She said there was specific demand for textile, automobile firms and the Steel Authority of India Ltd.
"There was demand from both U.S. and Far East buyers," another dealer said.
The Cazenove GDR index was up 1.69 points or 2.17 percent to 79.57.
The Capel India GDR index was up 1.47 points or 2.10 percent to 71.69.
Dealers also reported buying orders on rumours of announcement of "sweeteners" with the forthcoming GDR issue of Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd.
VSNL's would be India's biggest ever GDR issue, with plans to raise more than 600 million dollars.
"These rumours were combined with hopes of a more reform-friendly budget," one emerging market analyst.
India's finance minister P. Chidambaram, a keen supporter of market reforms, is due to present the central budget on February 28.
Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company rose 44 cents to 11.25 dollars while engineering firm Larsen & Toubro gained 48 cents at 14.375.
Taiwanese shares held firm as rumours about health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping faded on Wednesday.
"There was selective demand, mainly to cover short positions," a trader said.
Analysts expect Taiwanese shares to remain sluggish until Chinese officials announced anything categorical on Deng's health.
The Capel Taiwanese GDR index was up by just 0.40 points or 0.39 percent to 101.96.
The Capel Korea index was down 0.76 points or 1.17 percent on fears of lower than anticipated earnings in select blue chip shares.
"Electronic shares were under selling pressure," a dealer said.
